latest_teacher_action.diagnosis: The previous prompt preserved object presence, colors, and the koalas-in-front relation, but it was too loose for the two larger counted groups. 'Arranged behind them' and 'a separate visible group to the side' allowed the model to compress, merge, or partially hide individual trumpets and giraffes, which likely reduced countability. The count failures are persistent, so the next prompt should switch to a stricter layout with clearly separated rows and explicit left-to-right countable instances.
expected_improvement: Increase recognizability of exactly six pink trumpets by placing all six as separate full instruments in one visible back row behind the koalas.
Increase recognizability of exactly five brown giraffes by placing all five as separate full giraffes in one visible side row with gaps between them.
Preserve the already-correct four yellow koalas and the koalas-in-front-of-trumpets relation while reducing overlap and crowding.
preserve_constraints: The four yellow koalas are in front of the trumpets.
Koalas, trumpets, and giraffes are all present.

previous_plan_error.details: The prior plan used general grouping language but did not force each trumpet and each giraffe to be fully visible, separated, and individually countable. It also allowed the behind/side groups to be crowded or partially obscured by the foreground koalas.

latest_teacher_action.regeneration_strategy: Use a simple wide composition with three clearly separated groups: a back row of six pink trumpets, a front row of four yellow koalas directly in front of that trumpet row, and a side row of five brown giraffes. Require full-body/full-object visibility, left-to-right spacing, and visible gaps so every instance can be counted without overlap or merging. Keep the scene minimal and uncluttered to avoid extra detections.
regression_risks: Making the trumpets too large or too close to the koalas could break the front/behind relation or hide some trumpets.
Pushing the giraffes too far to the side could crop them or make them too small to count.
Overemphasizing separation without restating colors could risk attribute drift, so color binding must remain explicit.
repair_constraints: Show exactly six pink trumpets as six separate, fully visible instruments in a single horizontal back row behind the koalas, with visible gaps between neighboring trumpets.
Show exactly five brown giraffes as five separate, fully visible giraffes in a single side group, spaced apart so each giraffe is individually countable.
Keep exactly four yellow koalas in the foreground in front of the trumpet row, with only minimal overlap so the trumpets remain visible behind them.
Do not include any extra koalas, extra trumpets, or extra giraffes.
Keep the scene uncluttered so no required object is cropped, merged, tiny, or hidden.

To one side, show exactly five brown giraffes in a separate visible row, five fully visible distinct giraffes with space between each one. Make every koala, trumpet, and giraffe large enough to count easily, with minimal overlap and no cropping. Keep the relation clear: the four yellow koalas are in front of the six pink trumpets. No extra koalas, no extra trumpets, no extra giraffes.

Keep the scene minimal and uncluttered to avoid extra detections.
